chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you,' he said: 'Lentils and chickpeas and other than that.'

key_terms.الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ: those who were given the Scripture (People of the Book)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'food of the People of the Book is lawful for you' specifically refer to according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a specific juristic interpretation of Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:5, limiting the permissibility of 'food of the People of the Book' to plant-based items like lentils and chickpeas, thereby excluding meat. This view contrasts with other Shia scholars who include meat, highlighting the diversity of ijtihad in interpreting the term 'ta'am' within the context of dietary laws. The hadith underscores the principle that while general permissibility exists, specific restrictions may apply based on the nature of the food and the practices of the People of the Book.
